title: What is the difference between a loan interest rate and the APR? — Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, Ask CFPB
subject: finance
attribution: Source material: Consumer Financial Protection Bureau, Ask CFPB, 'What is the difference between a loan interest rate and the APR?'. Information created by the CFPB is in the public domain. The Consumer Financial Protection Bureau has not reviewed, approved or endorsed this activity.
transcription: Main answer text only (the 'Auto loans' breadcrumb, 'last reviewed: AUG 28, 2026' line, 'Don't see what you're looking for?' related-questions block, 'Page last modified' stamp, About-us sidebar and Legal disclaimer footer removed). Section headings ('Interest rate', 'Annual Percentage Rate (APR)', 'How to get the best rates', 'What lenders are required to provide') kept as plain lines; the in-answer 'Know before you shop' promo paragraph and its closing link line kept as printed. Inline links flattened to their text. Curly apostrophes kept. Whitespace normalised.
purpose: library: interest rate versus APR — two measures of the price of borrowing compared (the interest rate is the yearly cost of the money alone; the APR is the rate plus lender fees such as origination charges, both as percentages), credit-score and rate-shopping guidance, and the Truth in Lending Act requirement that lenders disclose the APR before finalising an auto loan. Fits a compare table (interest rate vs APR) and quiz cards with predict-then-reveal.
